    44	results are missing and why. See [Connect-Maester](connect-maester/readme.md).
    45	
    46	## Step 2: Read the report
    47	
    48	When the run finishes, Maester writes an HTML report to the `./test-results` folder and, in an interactive session, opens it. Every test appears with one
    49	of these results:
    50	
    51	| Result | What it means |
    52	| --- | --- |
    53	| **Passed** | The setting matches what the test expects. |
    54	| **Failed** | The setting does not match. The test explains why and how to fix it. |
    55	| **Investigate** | Maester found something a person should look at; it cannot decide on its own. |
    56	| **Skipped** | The test did not run, for example because a service is not connected, a licence is missing or a permission was not granted. |
    57	| **Error** | The test could not finish, for example because a service returned an unexpected error. |
    58	| **Not run** | The test was left out of this run, for example because your configuration turned it off. The reason is shown. |
    59	
    60	Each failed test links to its own page on this site, with the background, the fix and the references.
    61	
    62	## Step 3: Fix what matters first
    63	
    64	A first report usually has many failures. Do not try to fix them all at once.
    65	
    66	1. **Sort by severity.** Start with **Critical** and **High** (see [Severity levels](configuration/severity-levels.md)).
    67	   To run only those tests:
    68	
    69	   ```powershell
    70	   Invoke-Maester -Severity Critical, High
    71	   ```
    72	
    73	2. **Look for quick wins.** Each test says how much its fix affects users and how much effort it takes. A failure
    74	   with high severity, low user impact and low cost is the best place to start. In an interactive run, the
    75	   **Fix first** panel lists these failures for you.
    76	3. **Record what you accept.** Some failures are deliberate decisions. Turn those tests off in your configuration
    77	   with a reason, so the report shows them as **Not run** with your reason instead of as failures (see the next
    78	   step).
    79	
    80	## Step 4: Tell Maester about your tenant
    81	
    82	Create a folder for your Maester settings and a `maester-config.json` in it. The most important setting is your
    83	emergency access (break glass) accounts, which many Conditional Access tests depend on:
    84	
    85	```json
    86	{
    87	  "GlobalSettings": {
    88	    "EmergencyAccessAccounts": [
    89	      { "Type": "User", "UserPrincipalName": "BreakGlass1@contoso.com" }
    90	    ]
    91	  }
    92	}
    93	```
    94	
    95	Then run Maester from that folder, or pass it with `-Path`:
    96	
    97	```powershell
    98	Invoke-Maester -Path ./maester
    99	```
   100	
   101	When you have decided to accept a failure, add a `TestSettings` row for that test with your reason. Add one only
   102	for a decision that has been made, because the test then stops checking that setting:
   103	
   104	```json
   105	{
   106	  "TestSettings": [
   107	    { "Id": "<test ID>", "Enabled": false, "Reason": "<the decision and where it is recorded, for example RISK-042>" }
   108	  ]
   109	}
   110	```
   111	
   112	See [Configure Maester](configuration/overview.md) and [Emergency access accounts](configuration/emergency-access-accounts.md).
   113	
   114	## Step 5: Choose your baseline
   115	
   116	Maester ships several suites: its own tests and the CIS, CISA, ASD Essential Eight, EIDSCA and ORCA suites. Pick the ones that match
   117	the requirements your organisation has to meet. See [Choosing a baseline](choosing-a-baseline.md).
   118	
   119	## Step 6: Monitor continuously
   120	
   121	A single report shows where you stand today. The value of Maester comes from running it every day, so that a change
   122	that weakens your security is caught within a day instead of at the next audit.
   123	
   124	1. Run Maester on a schedule from a pipeline or an Azure service. See [Monitoring with Maester](monitoring/readme.mdx).
   125	2. Send the results to the people who act on them by email, Teams or Slack. See [Maester alerts](alerts/readme.mdx).
   126	3. Export results for a ticketing system or a spreadsheet. See [Exporting results](export-results.md).
   127	
   128	## Step 7: Add your own tests
   129	
   130	The built-in tests check widely recommended settings. Your organisation also has its own rules: a group that must
   131	always be in a policy, a named location that must exist, an app that must never get more permissions. Write those
   132	rules as [custom tests](writing-tests/index.mdx) and Maester checks them on every run alongside the built-in ones.
   133	
   134	## Next steps
   135	
   136	- Need support from leadership to roll this out? See [Making the case for Maester](making-the-case.mdx).
   137	- Questions? See the [FAQ](faq.md).

1	---
     2	title: Choosing a baseline
     3	description: The test suites that ship with Maester, which requirements each one serves, and how to run the combination that fits your organisation.
     4	---
     5	
     6	# Choosing a baseline
     7	
     8	Maester does not pick a security framework for you. It ships several suites of tests, each built from a different
     9	source, and you run the ones that match the requirements your organisation has to meet. This page explains what
    10	each suite is, helps you match suites to your requirements, and shows how to make your choice the default for every
    11	run.
    12	
    13	## The suites that ship with Maester
    14	
    15	| Suite | Source | What it checks | `-Suite` |
    16	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
    17	| [Maester](/docs/tests/maester) | The Maester community | Entra ID, Conditional Access, privileged access, app registrations, Exchange, Teams, Defender, Intune, Azure DevOps, AI agents and more. Written from real attacks and misconfigurations seen in tenants. | `Maester` |
    18	| [CIS](/docs/tests/cis) | [CIS Microsoft 365 Foundations Benchmark](https://www.cisecurity.org/benchmark/microsoft_365) and CIS GitHub Benchmark | The benchmark's recommendations that can be read from the service. A few need a person to confirm them and report **Investigate**. Each result names its recommendation and its level, L1 or L2. | `CIS` |
    19	| [CISA](/docs/tests/cisa) | [CISA SCuBA](https://github.com/cisagov/ScubaGear) Secure Configuration Baselines | The automatable SCuBA policies for Entra ID, Exchange Online and SharePoint Online. Each requirement carries its NIST SP 800-53 references. | `CISA` |
    20	| [ASD](/docs/tests/asd) | [ASD Essential Eight maturity model](https://www.cyber.gov.au/business-government/asds-cyber-security-frameworks/essential-eight/essential-eight-maturity-model) and [Information security manual](https://www.cyber.gov.au/ism) (ISM) | Entra ID and Intune settings for the Essential Eight requirements and ISM controls that can be read from Microsoft 365, such as phishing-resistant MFA, just-in-time administration and Office macro hardening. Each result names its ISM control and, for Essential Eight, the maturity level and mitigation strategy. | `ASD` |
    21	| [EIDSCA](/docs/tests/eidsca) | [Entra ID Security Config Analyzer](https://github.com/Cloud-Architekt/AzureAD-Attack-Defense) | Entra ID tenant settings (authorisation, consent, authentication methods, password protection) against recommended values. | `EIDSCA` |
    22	| [ORCA](/docs/tests/orca) | [Office 365 Recommended Configuration Analyzer](https://github.com/cammurray/orca) | Exchange Online Protection and Defender for Office 365: anti-spam, anti-phishing, Safe Links, Safe Attachments. | `ORCA` |
    23	| [Active Directory](/docs/tests/ad) | The Maester community | On-premises Active Directory inventory and configuration. Runs only after `Connect-Maester -Service ActiveDirectory`. | `AD` |
    24	
    25	[Maester Packs](packs/index.md) add more, for example the [Zero Trust Assessment pack](packs/zero-trust-assessment.md),
    26	which runs Microsoft's Zero Trust Assessment and shows its results in the same report.
    27	
    28	By default, `Invoke-Maester` runs every built-in suite except Active Directory, and leaves out preview and
    29	long-running tests.
    30	
    31	## Match suites to your requirements
    32	
    33	Start from what your organisation has to show, not from the suites. Most organisations combine two or three rows.
    34	
    35	| If your requirement is… | Run | Why |
    36	| --- | --- | --- |
    37	| Evidence against the CIS Microsoft 365 Foundations Benchmark (an auditor, an insurer, a customer questionnaire) | `CIS` | Each result names its CIS recommendation and level. |
    38	| Alignment with CISA SCuBA, or a control set built on NIST SP 800-53 | `CISA` | Each result names its SCuBA policy, and the NIST controls it relates to. |
    39	| Alignment with the ASD Essential Eight or the ISM (Australian government and organisations that follow ASD guidance) | `ASD` | Each result names its ISM control, and for Essential Eight the maturity level (ML1 to ML3) and mitigation strategy. A passing check is evidence for its control, not an Essential Eight assessment. |
    40	| An internal standard, or a framework Maester does not ship (ISO/IEC 27001, NIST CSF, a sector regulation) | `Maester`, `EIDSCA`, plus your own tests mapped to that framework | Maester's tests cover the technical settings most frameworks ask for. Map your own tests to your framework's requirements (see [below](#your-own-framework)). |
    41	| Hardening Entra ID against identity attacks | `Maester`, `EIDSCA` | Conditional Access, privileged access, consent and authentication settings. |
    42	| Reducing phishing and malware by email | `ORCA`, and the Exchange and Defender tests of `Maester` | Mail flow protection and its policies. |
    43	| A Zero Trust programme | The [Zero Trust Assessment pack](packs/zero-trust-assessment.md) and `Maester` | Microsoft's assessment by Zero Trust pillar, with Maester's checks in the same report. |
    44	| Hybrid identity with on-premises Active Directory | `AD`, alongside the others | The on-premises side of the identity that Entra ID trusts. |
    45	| No formal requirement yet | Everything (the default) | You see the whole picture and narrow it down later. |
    46	
    47	### Overlap between suites
    48	
    49	Several suites check the same setting from their own source. For example, blocking legacy authentication is
    50	checked by [MT.1009](/docs/tests/MT.1009), [CIS.M365.5.2.2.3](/docs/tests/CIS.M365.5.2.2.3) and the CISA
    51	suite. That is expected: each result reports against its own framework. If you need one framework view, run its
    52	suite. To add tests from other suites, run them in a separate invocation that names their own suite, for example
    53	`Invoke-Maester -Suite Maester -TestId MT.1009`. The selectors must all match, so `-Suite CIS -TestId MT.1009` runs
    54	nothing, and leaving `-Suite` out does not help when your configuration sets `Selection.Suite`: the configured suite
    55	still applies.
    56	
    57	## Make your choice the default
    58	
    59	Run a combination on the command line:
    60	
    61	```powershell
    62	Invoke-Maester -Suite CIS, Maester
    63	```
    64	
    65	Or save it in the `Selection` section of `maester-config.json`, so every run, including scheduled ones, uses the
    66	same baseline:
    67	
    68	```json
    69	{
    70	  "Selection": {
    71	    "Suite": ["CIS", "Maester"]
    72	  }
    73	}
    74	```
    75	
    76	Selectors combine: values of one selector are alternatives, different selectors must all match. To focus on the most
    77	urgent tests of your baseline first:
    78	
    79	```powershell
    80	Invoke-Maester -Suite CISA -Severity Critical, High
    81	```
    82	
    83	See the [run configuration reference](configuration/run-configuration.md) for every key of `Selection`, and
    84	[Invoke-Maester](commands/Invoke-Maester.mdx) for all the selectors (`-Product`, `-Feature`, `-Area`, `-Severity`,
    85	`-Suite`, `-TestId`).
    86	
    87	## Adapt the baseline to your organisation
    88	
    89	No baseline fits an organisation without changes. Record your decisions in `maester-config.json`, so they are
    90	visible and reviewed rather than ignored:
    91	
    92	- **A recommendation you have decided not to follow:** turn the test off with a reason. The report shows it as
    93	  **Not run** with your reason, so an auditor can see the decision.
    94	- **A risk that matters more or less to you:** change the test's severity.
    95	- **A threshold that differs from the default:** change the test's parameters.
    96	
    97	```json
    98	{
    99	  "TestSettings": [
   100	    { "Id": "CIS.M365.1.3.3", "Enabled": false, "Reason": "Calendar sharing approved by risk committee, RISK-042" },
   101	    { "Id": "MT.1005", "Severity": "Critical" },
   102	    { "Id": "MT.1198", "Parameters": { "MaximumValidityDays": 180 } }
   103	  ]
   104	}
   105	```
   106	
   107	Keep this file in version control so that every change to your baseline has an author, a date and a review.
   108	See [Configure Maester](configuration/overview.md).
   109	
   110	## Your own framework
   111	
   112	If your organisation has its own standard, or follows a framework Maester does not ship, write tests for the
   113	requirements Maester does not already cover and map each one to its requirement with the `Control` attribute. A
   114	framework file in your suite gives Maester the framework's name, version and requirements, and every result then
   115	names the requirement it implements. See
   116	[Benchmarks and framework files](writing-tests/index.mdx#benchmarks-and-framework-files).
   117	
   118	Many built-in tests already name the NIST SP 800-53 controls they support in their `Control` attribute, and most
   119	frameworks publish a mapping to NIST SP 800-53, which helps you find the built-in tests that serve a requirement.

     8	# Making the case for Maester
     9	
    10	Maester is free, but rolling it out still needs someone's time, a place to run it and, often, approval. This page
    11	helps you get that approval. It has three parts:
    12	
    13	1. [What organisations miss without continuous monitoring](#what-organisations-miss-without-continuous-monitoring):

    26	## What organisations miss without continuous monitoring
    27	
    28	A Microsoft 365 tenant changes every week: people join and leave, admins grant exceptions, projects add apps, and
    29	Microsoft releases new features with new settings. Most security weaknesses in a tenant are not the result of an
    30	attack. They are a setting that was right once, and was then changed, or quietly stopped working, without anyone

    32	changed.

**It's nearly ready to merge. Three one-line wording fixes are left, and then it's good to go.** The pages are accurate, read well and are aimed at the right people.

## Do the docs make sense?

Yes. Each page has one clear job:

- **Getting started**: install → read the report → fix Critical/High first → config → baseline → monitor → custom tests. It's the path new users are missing today, and it links to the detailed pages instead of copying them. The results table (Passed / Failed / Investigate / Skipped / Error / Not run) is the most useful part.
- **Choosing a baseline**: it doesn't push one framework. The "If your requirement is… → Run" table is the right way in, and the section on how suites overlap answers a question people ask often.
- **Making the case**: the "what goes unnoticed" table is strong. The executive, CISO and ITSA templates are long, but they're tabbed and meant to be copied, so the length is fine. The ITSA template is unusually honest about SharePoint full control, `-Privileged`, the limits of redaction and telemetry. That will help it get through a security review.

## Fact check

I checked the pages against the code:
- **Test IDs:** all 24 cited exist and match what the pages say about them.
- **Switches:** every switch named exists on `Invoke-Maester`, `Connect-Maester` or `Get-MtGraphScope`.
- **Behaviour claims:**
  - MT.1076 really does turn report obfuscation off and back on.
  - MT.1199 is long-running.
  - MT.1198 has the `MaximumValidityDays` parameter.
  - The telemetry description matches `Write-Telemetry.ps1`.
  - The "Fix first" panel exists.
- **Your earlier review:** all six points were addressed.
- **CI:** green.

## Fix before merge

These are 3 of the 4 CodeRabbit threads still open from Nov 8. They were posted after the author's last push.

## Optional modules and permissions

Maester includes optional [CISA](tests/cisa/) tests that require additional permissions and modules to run. These optional tests are skipped if the modules are not installed or there is no active connection.

> Also see [Create-entra-app](sections/create-entra-app.md)

### Installing Azure, Exchange Online, Teams and PnP.PowerShell modules

```powershell
Install-Module Az.Accounts, ExchangeOnlineManagement, MicrosoftTeams, PnP.PowerShell -Scope CurrentUser
```

> The Security & Compliance PowerShell module is dependent on the ExchangeOnlineManagement `Connect-IPPSSession` cmdlet.

### Connecting to Azure, Exchange, and other services

In order to run all the CISA tests, you need to connect to the Azure, Exchange Online, and other modules.

For a more detailed introduction to these concepts see the [Connect-Maester](connect-maester/readme.md) documentation.

Run the following command to interactively connect to the Azure, Microsoft Graph, Exchange Online, and other modules. A sign-in window will appear for each module.

```powershell
Connect-Maester -Service All
```

### Connecting to GitHub

GitHub is an optional connection for GitHub security tests and is not included in `Connect-Maester -Service All`.
For interactive sessions, use the Maester GitHub App OAuth flow:

```powershell
Connect-Maester -Service Graph,GitHub -GitHubOrganization '<github-organization>'
```

See [Connect to GitHub (optional)](connect-maester/readme.md#connect-to-github-optional) for GitHub App install/approval details and token-based automation options.

### Permissions

Exchange Online implements a [role-based access control model](https://learn.microsoft.com/exchange/permissions-exo/permissions-exo). The controls these cmdlets test require minimum roles of either of the following:

* View-Only Configuration OR
* O365SupportViewConfig

### Installing Azure DevOps PowerShell module

```powershell
Install-Module ADOPS -Scope CurrentUser
```

### Connecting to Azure DevOps

In order to run all the Azure DevOps tests, you need to connect to Azure DevOps.

This is currently not included as part of [Connect-Maester](connect-maester/readme.md) and must be called separately. Run the following command to interactively connect using the Azure DevOps modules. A sign-in window will appear.

Example with PowerShell variable
```powershell
$AdoPSAllowInsecureAPIs = $true
Import-Module ADOPS
Connect-ADOPS -Organization <Name Of DevOps Organization>
```

Example with ArgumentList
```powershell
Import-Module ADOPS -ArgumentList $true
Connect-ADOPS -Organization <Name Of DevOps Organization>
```

> Note: Some of the API endpoints used for Azure DevOps tests use unsupported endpoints.
To allow usage of unsupported endpoints, you must set `$true` in the argumentlist when importing the module, or set a PowerShell variable called "$AdoPSAllowInsecureAPIs" to `$true` before importing the module.
Reference: https://github.com/AZDOPS/AZDOPS/issues/248

### Permissions

Azure DevOps implements a [role-based access control model](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/organizations/security/permissions?view=azure-devops&tabs=preview-page). The controls these cmdlets test require the minimum role of:

* Project-Scoped Users at Organization level

### Connect to SharePoint Online (optional)

Maester includes SharePoint Online security tests that use the [PnP PowerShell](https://pnp.github.io/powershell/) module.

Install the PnP PowerShell module if you haven't already:

```powershell
Install-Module PnP.PowerShell -Scope CurrentUser
```

A dedicated Entra ID app registration configured for PnP interactive login is required. The easiest way to create one is to follow the official [PnP app registration guide](https://pnp.github.io/powershell/articles/registerapplication.html) and run `Register-PnPEntraIDAppForInteractiveLogin`, which outputs the **Client ID** you will supply to `-SharePointClientId`. For the Maester-specific SharePoint permission setup, see [Grant permissions to SharePoint Online](../sections/create-entra-app.md).


Connect to SharePoint Online together with Microsoft Graph (the admin URL is auto-discovered from your tenant's initial domain):

```powershell
Connect-Maester -Service Graph,SharePointOnline -SharePointClientId '<Client ID>'
```

If auto-discovery does not work (e.g. in government or custom-domain tenants), supply the admin URL explicitly:

```powershell
Connect-Maester -Service Graph,SharePointOnline -SharePointClientId '<Client ID>' -SharePointAdminUrl 'https://contoso-admin.sharepoint.com'
```

If the PnP PowerShell module is not installed or there is no active connection, all SharePoint Online tests are skipped automatically.

### Connect to Azure, Exchange Online, Copilot Studio and Teams
### Connect to Azure DevOps (optional)

Maester includes an *optional* set of Azure DevOps security tests (AZDO.*).
These tests require the community [`ADOPS`](https://www.powershellgallery.com/packages/ADOPS) PowerShell module and an active connection to your Azure DevOps organization.

Connecting to Azure DevOps is **not** part of `Connect-Maester` and must be done separately:

```powershell
Install-Module ADOPS -Scope CurrentUser
Connect-ADOPS -Organization <your-organization>
```

If the `ADOPS` module is not installed or there is no active connection, the Azure DevOps tests are skipped automatically.

See the [installation guide](../installation.md#installing-azure-devops-powershell-module) for prerequisites and permissions, and the [Azure DevOps tests for Maester](/blog/azuredevops-tests-for-maester) blog post for the full list of available tests.

content.text:
**We still need the URL, but not the page as it is now.** The content can shrink to a short reference page, because most of it repeats Getting started or the [Connect-Maester](website/docs/connect-maester/readme.md) docs.

## Why the page can't just be deleted
`/docs/installation` is the site's main entry point:
- The header's **Get started** button and **Install** link, and the homepage **Quickstart →** button, all point to it (`SiteLayout.astro`, `index.astro`).
- The 404 page and six docs pages link to it.
- It's covered by the URL contract check.

Those buttons should now point to `/docs/getting-started`.

## What's only in the install guide
| Content | Elsewhere? |
| --- | --- |
| Windows PowerShell 5.1 is not supported | No |
| Tests ship inside the module, no folder needed | No |
| Pester is only needed for Pester-format custom tests | No |
| One `Install-Module` line for the Az, Exchange, Teams and PnP modules | Only PnP and ADOPS appear in Connect-Maester |
| Security & Compliance PowerShell comes with the ExchangeOnlineManagement module | No |
| Exchange roles for interactive runs (View-Only Configuration / O365SupportViewConfig) | Only for app-only runs (Connect-Maester advanced page) |
| Azure DevOps: the `$AdoPSAllowInsecureAPIs` flag and the minimum role | No; the Connect-Maester page links here for them |
| Install, connect, run; the `-Path` folder; connecting to Exchange, Teams, SharePoint and GitHub | Yes, in Getting started or Connect-Maester |

## Stale or wrong today
- **Wrong framing:** it calls the optional modules "optional CISA tests". They serve the Exchange, Teams and SharePoint tests in every suite.
- **Missing SharePoint setup:** Getting started says Installation covers `-SharePointClientId`, but it doesn't mention it.
- **Broken anchors:** `sections/create-entra-app.mdx` links to two anchors that no longer exist (`#installing-azure-and-exchange-online-modules`, `#installing-azure-exchange-online-and-teams-modules`).

## Proposed rewrite
1. **Make Installation a short reference** with:

title: Active Directory Connection Troubleshooting
description: "Fix Active Directory connection errors in Maester: TLS modes (LDAPS and StartTLS), domain controller certificate problems, the Linux and macOS StartTLS limit, and verbose diagnostics."
sidebar:

## Overview
- Maester uses System.DirectoryServices.Protocols.LdapConnection for cross-platform AD connectivity.
- TLS is required for all AD connections.
## Understanding TLS Modes
- The -ActiveDirectoryTlsMode parameter supports three values: Auto, Ldaps, StartTls.
- Auto (default): Tries LDAPS (port 636) first, then StartTLS (port 389) on Windows. On Linux/macOS, only tries LDAPS.
- Ldaps: Uses LDAPS on port 636 only.
- StartTls: Uses StartTLS on port 389 only.
- Auto mode adapts to the platform due to a known .NET limitation.
## Certificate Issues on the Domain Controller
- Common symptoms: connection fails with certificate, trust, validation, expired, or chain errors.
- Troubleshooting steps:
  1. Verify the DC has a valid server-authentication certificate installed.
  2. Verify the certificate SAN includes the DC's FQDN.
  3. Verify the certificate is not expired.
  4. On the client, verify the DC's certificate chain is trusted.
  5. For test environments only: use `Connect-Maester -Service ActiveDirectory -ActiveDirectorySkipCertificateCheck` to bypass certificate validation.
- If LDAPS fails but StartTLS succeeds, the DC's LDAPS certificate (port 636) is misconfigured — check the certificate on the DC.

import InstallCommand from '@components/InstallCommand.astro';

This page is the reference for installing Maester and the modules its tests use. To go from nothing to your first
report, follow [Getting started](getting-started.mdx).

## Requirements

- **PowerShell 7.4 or later** on Windows, Linux or macOS. Windows PowerShell 5.1 is not supported.
- An account that can read your tenant's configuration, such as Global Reader. See
  [Connect-Maester](connect-maester/readme.md).

## Install Maester

<InstallCommand />

The tests ship inside the module, so there is nothing else to download and no folder to set up. Maester installs
`Microsoft.Graph.Authentication`, the only module it requires, with it.

You need a folder only to change settings or add your own tests. Put a `maester-config.json` (see
[Configuration](configuration/overview.md)) and a `custom` folder for your tests (see
[Writing custom tests](writing-tests/index.mdx)) in it, and run `Invoke-Maester -Path <folder>` or run Maester from
that folder.

Upgrading from Maester 2.x? See [Upgrading from 2.x](upgrading-from-2x.md).

## Update or pin a version

Update to the latest release:

```powershell
Update-Module Maester
```

Add `-AllowPrerelease` to update to the latest preview.

For scheduled runs, pin a version so a new release changes your results only when you choose. Read the
[release notes](https://github.com/maester365/maester/releases), then install the version you have reviewed:

```powershell
Install-Module Maester -RequiredVersion <version> -Scope CurrentUser
```

## Optional modules and permissions

`Connect-Maester` connects to Microsoft Graph, which is enough for the Entra ID tests and most of the others. The
tests for the services below need their own module. A test whose module is missing, or whose service is not
connected, is reported as **Skipped** with the reason, and `Connect-Maester` shows the command to install the
missing module.

| Service | Module | Connect | Permissions |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Azure, Copilot Studio (Dataverse) | `Az.Accounts` | [`-Service Azure`, `Dataverse`](connect-maester/readme.md#connect-to-azure-exchange-online-copilot-studio-and-teams) | Reader on the subscriptions the tests read |
| Exchange Online, Security & Compliance | `ExchangeOnlineManagement` | [`-Service EXO`](connect-maester/readme.md#connect-to-azure-exchange-online-copilot-studio-and-teams) | See [Exchange Online](#exchange-online) |
| Microsoft Teams | `MicrosoftTeams` | [`-Service Teams`](connect-maester/readme.md#connect-to-azure-exchange-online-copilot-studio-and-teams) | A reader role such as Global Reader |
| SharePoint Online | `PnP.PowerShell`, plus an app registration | [`-SharePointClientId`](connect-maester/readme.md#connect-to-sharepoint-online-optional) | [Grant permissions to SharePoint Online](sections/create-entra-app.md) |
| GitHub | None | [`-Service GitHub`](connect-maester/readme.md#connect-to-github-optional) | The Maester GitHub App, or a token |
| Azure DevOps | `ADOPS` | [`Connect-ADOPS`](connect-maester/readme.md#connect-to-azure-devops-optional) | See [Azure DevOps](#azure-devops) |
| Active Directory | None | [`-Service ActiveDirectory`](connect-maester/readme.md) | A domain account that can read the directory |

Install the Microsoft 365 modules in one go:

```powershell
Install-Module Az.Accounts, ExchangeOnlineManagement, MicrosoftTeams, PnP.PowerShell -Scope CurrentUser
```

Then connect to all of them. GitHub, Azure DevOps and Active Directory are not part of `All` and are connected
separately.

```powershell
Connect-Maester -Service All -SharePointClientId '<Client ID>'
```

### Exchange Online

Exchange Online has its own [role-based access control](https://learn.microsoft.com/exchange/permissions-exo/permissions-exo).
The Exchange tests need one of these roles:

- View-Only Configuration
- O365SupportViewConfig

The Security & Compliance tests use `Connect-IPPSSession` from the same `ExchangeOnlineManagement` module. For
unattended runs, see [Connect-Maester advanced](connect-maester/connect-maester-advanced.mdx).

### Azure DevOps

The Azure DevOps tests need the minimum role of **Project-Scoped Users** at the organization level. Some of the
endpoints they call are ones the `ADOPS` module marks as unsupported, so allow them when you import it. See
[Connect to Azure DevOps](connect-maester/readme.md#connect-to-azure-devops-optional).

## Pester

Maester 3.0 does not need Pester. Install it only if you have custom tests written in the Pester format
(`*.Tests.ps1`), see [Pester-format tests](writing-tests/pester-format-tests.md):

```powershell
Install-Module Pester -MinimumVersion 5.7.1 -SkipPublisherCheck -Force -Scope CurrentUser
```

## Next steps

- [Getting started](getting-started.mdx): your first report, and the steps from there to continuous monitoring.
- [Connect-Maester](connect-maester/readme.md): every way to connect, including unattended runs.
- [Monitoring with Maester](monitoring/readme.mdx): run Maester on a schedule.

For scheduled runs, pin a version so that a new release changes your results only when you choose. Read the
[release notes](https://github.com/maester365/maester/releases), then install the version you reviewed:

```powershell
Install-Module Maester -RequiredVersion <version> -Scope CurrentUser
```

## Optional modules and permissions

`Connect-Maester` connects to Microsoft Graph, which is enough for the Entra ID tests and most of the others. The
tests for the services below need a module or a connection of their own. When one is missing, its tests are
reported as **Skipped** with the reason, and `Connect-Maester` shows the command that installs the missing module.

| Service | Module | How to connect | Permissions |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Azure, Copilot Studio (Dataverse) | `Az.Accounts` | [Connect-Maester](connect-maester/readme.md#connect-to-azure-exchange-online-copilot-studio-and-teams) | [Azure](sections/create-entra-app.md#optional-grant-permissions-to-azure), [Dataverse](sections/create-entra-app.md#optional-grant-dataverse-permissions-for-copilot-studio) |
| Exchange Online, Security & Compliance | `ExchangeOnlineManagement` | [Connect-Maester](connect-maester/readme.md#connect-to-azure-exchange-online-copilot-studio-and-teams) | [Exchange Online](#exchange-online) |
| Microsoft Teams | `MicrosoftTeams` | [Connect-Maester](connect-maester/readme.md#connect-to-azure-exchange-online-copilot-studio-and-teams) | [Teams](sections/create-entra-app.md#optional-grant-permissions-to-teams) |
| SharePoint Online | `PnP.PowerShell`, and an app registration whose client ID you pass with `-SharePointClientId` | [Connect to SharePoint Online](connect-maester/readme.md#connect-to-sharepoint-online-optional) | [SharePoint Online](sections/create-entra-app.md#optional-grant-permissions-to-sharepoint-online) |
| GitHub | None | [Connect to GitHub](connect-maester/readme.md#connect-to-github-optional) | The Maester GitHub App, or a token |
| Azure DevOps | `ADOPS` | [Connect to Azure DevOps](connect-maester/readme.md#connect-to-azure-devops-optional) | [Azure DevOps](#azure-devops) |
| Active Directory | None | `Connect-Maester -Service ActiveDirectory`, see [AD connection troubleshooting](connect-maester/ad-connection-troubleshooting.md) | |

Install the Microsoft 365 modules in one go:

```powershell
Install-Module Az.Accounts, ExchangeOnlineManagement, MicrosoftTeams, PnP.PowerShell -Scope CurrentUser
```

Then connect to all of them. GitHub, Azure DevOps and Active Directory are not part of `All`, so connect to them
separately.

```powershell
Connect-Maester -Service All -SharePointClientId '<Client ID>'
```

### Exchange Online

Exchange Online has its own [role-based access control](https://learn.microsoft.com/exchange/permissions-exo/permissions-exo).
The Exchange tests need one of these roles:

- View-Only Configuration
- O365SupportViewConfig

The Security & Compliance tests connect with `Connect-IPPSSession`, which comes with the same
`ExchangeOnlineManagement` module. For unattended runs, see
[Connect-Maester advanced](connect-maester/connect-maester-advanced.mdx).

### Azure DevOps

The Azure DevOps tests need the **Project-Scoped Users** role at the organization level, at least. Some of the
endpoints they call are ones the `ADOPS` module treats as unsupported, so allow them when you import the module (see
[Connect to Azure DevOps](connect-maester/readme.md#connect-to-azure-devops-optional)).

## Pester

Maester 3.0 does not need Pester. Install it only if you have custom tests written in the Pester format
(`*.Tests.ps1`), see [Pester-format tests](writing-tests/pester-format-tests.md):

```powershell
Install-Module Pester -MinimumVersion 5.7.1 -SkipPublisherCheck -Force -Scope CurrentUser
```

# Zero Trust Assessment pack

This pack runs Microsoft's [Zero Trust Assessment](https://aka.ms/zerotrust/assessment) and shows each of its
results in the Maester report, next to Maester's own checks. It ships with Maester and does not run unless you
ask for it.

Each assessment result is one row, `ZTA.<assessment test ID>` (for example `ZTA.21770`), with the
assessment's title, risk level (as the severity), description, remediation steps and findings. Results are tagged
`ZeroTrust` and `ZeroTrust.<pillar>` (`ZeroTrust.Identity`, `ZeroTrust.Devices` and so on).

Maester also places each result under the product, feature and security area it is about, such as Entra ID and
Conditional Access, and lists the MITRE ATT&CK techniques its control addresses, so assessment results appear
beside Maester's own checks in the report's product, area and ATT&CK views. The assessment does not record these,
so Maester keeps the mapping in the pack's `taxonomy.json`.

The pack's ID is `maester.zero-trust-assessment`. It needs no `Install-MtPack`: it is part of the Maester module,
and `Get-MtPack` lists it.

## Run it

Install the assessment's module once, connect Maester to the tenant, then name the pack. ZeroTrustAssessment 3.1.0 needs
PowerShell 7.6 or later (Maester itself runs on 7.4); on an older PowerShell the pack is skipped and says so.


```powershell
Install-Module ZeroTrustAssessment -Scope CurrentUser
Connect-Maester
Invoke-Maester -Pack ZTA -SkipBuiltIn    # only the Zero Trust Assessment
Invoke-Maester -Pack ZTA                 # Maester's tests and the assessment
```

You don't run `Connect-ZtAssessment` yourself. The assessment runs in a separate PowerShell process, which can't
use the sign-ins of your session, so Maester signs in there for you (see
[Let Maester run the assessment](#let-maester-run-the-assessment)). After an interactive `Connect-Maester` you

assessment which tenant to sign in to, and the pack is skipped while Maester is not connected to Graph. If you
read a report you already have (below), you run `Connect-ZtAssessment` and `Invoke-ZtAssessment` yourself first.

```powershell
Invoke-Maester -TestId ZTA          # only the Zero Trust Assessment
Invoke-Maester -Suite ZTA              # the same
Invoke-Maester -IncludeLongRunning          # everything, including the assessment
```

`Selection.IncludeLongRunning` to `true`. Give it time with `Execution.LongRunningTimeoutSeconds`: the assessment
can take an hour or more on a large tenant.
